title: A stream of stars over Paranal
caption: A stream of star trails over the Very Large Telescope, Paranal Observatory, Chile
celestial: Photograph taken at Paranal Observatory, Chile

recognition.text: ESO Picture of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: Smeared trails of starlight pour across the sky above ESO's Very Large Telescope (VLT) and its Auxiliary Telescopes at Paranal Observatory. Below the stream, the telescopes' own motion shows up as blurred flickers, while the stars' apparent drift across the sky, caused by Earth's rotation, leaves long streaks.

To get this result, ESO Photo Ambassador Gianluca Lombardi combined many long-exposure images. Stacking frames like this turns a long stretch of movement into a single picture. Paranal's sky, in the arid north of Chile, is a favourite with ESO's Photo Ambassadors, who keep trying out new techniques to capture better views of the landscape and the observatory's state-of-the-art facilities.
The VLT is ESO's flagship facility. ESO counts it among the most productive telescopes in the world and describes it as the most advanced optical instrument ever made.

understand.summary: This is a composite of many long-exposure photographs by Gianluca Lombardi. The source does not publish camera or colour-processing details.
understand.eye: An observer would see sharp stars and slowly moving telescopes, but combining long exposures smears both into trails and flickers.
